summary: Reduces the public login and signup transfer cost by restoring pnpm-aware frontend chunk boundaries and serving immutable assets with compression.
userImpact: Public login and signup visits download smaller compressed JavaScript and CSS responses while preserving existing authentication behavior.

notes: This frontend delivery change does not alter database schemas or persistence behavior.

security: Compression is limited to static JavaScript and CSS responses; existing content-security and immutable-cache headers remain enforced.
documentation: The release notes record the new frontend bundle budgets and compressed immutable-asset delivery behavior.
knownLimitations: This change improves transfer and cache behavior but does not remove the application bootstrap dependencies shared by public and authenticated routes.
rollback: Restore the previous Vite chunk classifier and Nginx static-asset block; no data rollback is required.
validation: Focused pnpm module-ID chunk-classification, frontend bundle-budget, Nginx delivery, and CI-classifier contract tests pass.
The production public login/signup graph passes with 1,143,241 gzip bytes of initial JavaScript and CSS; its largest initial JavaScript chunk is 2,319,552 raw bytes and 550,813 gzip bytes.
The pinned Nginx runtime returns Content-Encoding gzip and Vary Accept-Encoding for immutable JavaScript while preserving the one-year immutable cache policy.
The complete frontend suite passes 1,544 tests in 314 files, and the frontend-host suite passes 52 tests in 14 files.
